result.rationale: Verified in the diff: parseRefreshTokenResponse only applies the caller-provided `schema` when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is false; in sharing mode it uses `minimumTokenResponseSchema`, silently discarding per-app validation like googleCredentialSchema/refreshTokenResponseSchema/zoomRefreshedTokenSchema. judged_text: The function name and parameter promise schema-pluggability but in sharing mode the caller-provided schema is discarded entirely (minimumTokenResponseSchema wins), a parallel hidden branch that contradicts the signature contract `parseRefreshTokenResponse(response, schema)`. The next developer adding expiry/refresh_token validation to a per-app schema will see their validation silently ignored on shared deployments, and failures that the schema would have caught (missing expiry) pass green while the stored credential is unusable — a stand-in guard that goes green while the real contract is broken.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `parseRefreshTokenResponse(response, schema)` conditionally ignores the caller-provided `schema` when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is true, and instead validates only against `minimumTokenResponseSchema`. This is a real, diff-grounded “hidden branch” that makes the `schema` parameter ineffective in sharing mode and can surprise future callers expecting their per-app schema to be enforced.
